# Pinned continuation contracts and prototype gaps

This map is source-derived. It does not select an adapter surface or claim runtime behavior.

## Query basis and page identity

Public temporal input contains optional `recordedAt` and `validAt`; they are nonnegative finite epoch-millisecond values. The resolved query-page basis additionally carries a commit-position cut. On the first page the public layer obtains a current time and committed position; continuation restores the cursor's original basis. A newly sampled current position is not substituted into that restored basis. The public time/position reads are sequential, not wrapped in a read transaction at this call site; the adapter still owes the documented consistent committed boundary. See [Temporal](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Temporal.ts#L3-L51), [public query paging](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/TriplesLive.ts#L642-L671).

When both recorded cuts are present, the SQL compiler requires assertion time AND assertion position to be within their cuts. Retraction only hides a row when it has occurred by both cuts: a retraction beyond either cut does not hide it. Valid time remains inclusive-start/exclusive-end. Consequently neither a timestamp alone nor a position alone is a general replacement for the full page basis. See [compiler temporal predicate](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/datalog/compiler.ts#L171-L187).

The normalized query includes its page size and full projected-row tie-breaker. Cursor identity fingerprints that query and its resolved basis; the scope has a separate fingerprint. Scope uses a versioned tuple of environment, tenant, database and nonnegative safe-integer generation. It is an identity check, not tenant partitioning or authorization. Changing a page size is a query change at this pin. The encoding and fingerprints are not authentication: ordering values are carried in the envelope but are not hashed into its query/scope fingerprints. Do not treat an opaque cursor as an access-control capability. See [pagination](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Pagination.ts), [scope](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/runtime/DatabaseScope.ts).

The page executor receives one extra requested row. Only when actual results exceed the requested page size does finishing trim the extra row and construct a continuation from the last retained full ordering key. Query pages default to 100 and cap at 1000; constants-only set projections may have an empty ordering key and a terminal singleton. Typed mixed-family ordering, filters, inner logical limit/offset and language validation remain additional executor obligations, not features supplied merely by encoding a cursor.

## Global transaction journal and command receipts

The global `transactions({after,limit})` service validates a nonnegative safe-integer exclusive lower position and a 1–1000 page size, reads parsed transaction metadata, orders records by commit position, filters strictly above `after`, and slices the page. Every nonempty page returns its last position as `next`, including a short final page. An empty page has no next. Later commits can appear on a later request. This service does not have the query envelope's scope fingerprint or pinned upper position. See [journal service](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/TriplesLive.ts#L598-L622) and [metadata parser](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/transactionMetadata.ts).

This paragraph concerns the global service only. Entity-specific transaction history has a separate request/cut contract and is not interchangeable with that global continuation or an opaque query cursor.

`StorageAdapter.claimCommand(commandId,transactionId,timestamp)` must atomically reserve a command and return the original transaction ID for a duplicate. The standard write path checks this result before allocating a new commit position and raises the original-transaction duplicate error. Command ID is the idempotency identity; these paths do not validate a same-ID request by hashing its operations. Atomic rollback must encompass the claim, ordered position, facts/retractions and journal metadata. A duplicate error does not authorize replay. See [storage interface](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/storage/StorageAdapter.ts#L18-L39), [write path](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/TriplesLive.ts#L280-L298), [correctness contract](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/docs/custom-runtimes.md).

## Fixed clock and historical conformance

The standard deterministic runtime services return the supplied clock value on every call. Runtime composition forwards `deterministic.startTime` into those services. The conformance helper forwards the option and simply iterates its cases; no clock advance is inserted there. See [fixed clock](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/RuntimeServices.ts#L35-L43), [runtime composition](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/runtime/Runtime.ts#L64-L84), [suite forwarding](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/testkit/src/index.ts#L2865-L2886).

The historical-page case first asserts a,b,c, remembers their timestamp, sleeps, retracts b and asserts d, and only then captures its first page's position. Its expected a,b,c requires those changes to have later recorded timestamps. With a fixed clock and ordinary standard writes, they instead share the remembered timestamp and are already within that captured position; F01 derives a,c,d. Real waiting does not change an `Effect.succeed(fixedTime)` service. This conditional configuration mismatch is not an observed Triplex or DuckDB execution defect. The separate snapshot-stability case comments that mutation timestamps may tie but does not itself force ties. See [historical fixture](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/testkit/src/index.ts#L263-L294), [snapshot stability fixture](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/testkit/src/index.ts#L2784-L2851).

## Current DuckDB prototype mapping

| Requirement | Published schema 2 product source | Gap before a Triplex claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public recorded-time input plus exact position cut | `Query.known_at` is a logical position; timestamps are separate metadata | Do not alias `known_at` to `recordedAt`. Specify and implement the timestamp/position intersection. |
| Stable query continuation | Native reads return complete bounded relations and snapshot metadata | No Triplex paged query envelope, full keyset order or public executePage service is established. |
| Scoped database generation | Store owns a local experimental database with catalog/FP checks | No public DatabaseScope/generation cursor identity is exposed. A path or live pointer is not a replacement. |
| Original transaction-ID receipt | `td_commits` stores position, command_id and inserted_at; duplicate errors carry position | Preserve the caller/runtime transaction ID and transaction metadata explicitly; returning a position is not that contract. |
| Transaction journal | Ordered receipts and fact history exist | Receipt rows are not complete Triplex transaction records or change summaries. |
| Atomic recovery and lifecycle | Source uses one transaction for command mutation; bounded prior evidence is separate | Source shape does not prove rollback/COMMIT ambiguity, interruption, concurrency, crash recovery or release ownership. |
| Value/language compatibility | Disjoint string/bool/int64/finite-f64 prototype values and text Datalog | Triplex's tags and structural Datalog differ. No implicit coercion, tag equivalence or broad language support follows. |

Product anchors: [schema 2]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]), [query/commit data types]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]), [typed query]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]), [typed command/receipt/history]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]). Triplex anchors: [row](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Triple.ts), [value tags](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Value.ts), [executor](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/storage/QueryExecutor.ts).

Current commits are capped at 256, so their present position values fit the JavaScript safe-integer range. That bounded fact is not permission to silently convert arbitrary int64 values if the envelope is later widened. No stored database state was inspected for this map.
